sceneHappening: Five thousand fed, a walk on the sea, and the bread of life
summary: After this Jesus goes to the other side of the Sea of Galilee, which is also called the Sea of Tiberias. A great multitude follows him because they see the signs he does on the sick, and it is near the Passover. Seeing the crowd, Jesus asks Philip, "Where are we to buy bread, that these may eat?" He says this to test him, for he knows what he will do. Philip answers that two hundred denarii wouldn't buy enough bread for each to get a little. Andrew, Simon Peter's brother, says, "There is a boy here who has five barley loaves and two fish, but what are these among so many?" Jesus says, "Have the people sit down." There is much grass in the place, and the men sit, about five thousand. Jesus takes the loaves, gives thanks, and distributes them, and likewise the fish, as much as they want. When they are filled, he says, "Gather up the broken pieces which are left over, that nothing be lost," and they fill twelve baskets. When the people see the sign he has done, they say, "This is truly the prophet who comes into the world." Jesus, perceiving that they are about to come and take him by force to make him king, withdraws again to the mountain by himself. That evening the disciples go down to the sea, get into a boat, and head toward Capernaum. It is dark, and Jesus has not come to them, and the sea is rising with a great wind. When they have rowed about three or four miles, they see Jesus walking on the sea and drawing near the boat, and they are afraid. He says, "It is I. Don't be afraid." They are willing to receive him into the boat, and immediately the boat is at the land where they were going. The next day the crowd, finding that Jesus is not there, gets into boats and goes to Capernaum seeking him. When they find him they ask, "Rabbi, when did you come here?" Jesus says, "Most certainly I tell you, you seek me, not because you saw signs, but because you ate of the loaves, and were filled. Don't work for the food which perishes, but for the food which remains to eternal life, which the Son of Man will give to you." They ask, "What must we do, that we may work the works of God?" "This is the work of God, that you believe in him whom he has sent." They ask for a sign and mention the manna their fathers ate in the wilderness. Jesus says, "It wasn't Moses who gave you the bread from heaven, but my Father gives you the true bread from heaven. For the bread of God is that which comes down out of heaven, and gives life to the world." "Sir, always give us this bread." "I am the bread of life. He who comes to me will not be hungry, and he who believes in me will never be thirsty. ... All that the Father gives me will come to me. ... I have come down from heaven, not to do my own will, but the will of him who sent me. ... that everyone who sees the Son, and believes in him, should have eternal life; and I will raise him up at the last day." The Jews murmur, "Isn't this Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know?" Jesus says, "No one can come to me unless the Father who sent me draws him, and I will raise him up in the last day. ... I am the living bread which came down out of heaven. If anyone eats of this bread, he will live forever. Yes, the bread which I will give for the life of the world is my flesh." They argue, "How can this man give us his flesh to eat?" Jesus says, "Most certainly I tell you, unless you eat the flesh of the Son of Man and drink his blood, you have no life in yourselves. He who eats my flesh and drinks my blood has eternal life, and I will raise him up at the last day. ... It is the spirit who gives life. The flesh profits nothing. The words that I speak to you are spirit, and are life." He says this in the synagogue as he teaches at Capernaum. Many of his disciples say, "This is a hard saying! Who can listen to it?" and from that time many of them go back and no longer walk with him. Jesus asks the twelve, "You don't also want to go away, do you?" Simon Peter answers, "Lord, to whom would we go? You have the words of eternal life. We have come to believe and know that you are the Christ, the Son of the living God." Jesus answers, "Didn't I choose you, the twelve, and one of you is a devil?" John adds that he meant Judas the son of Simon Iscariot, who would betray him.
whySettingMatters: The feeding of the five thousand is the only miracle before the passion told in all four Gospels, and John uses it as the base for a long teaching. The setting is near the Passover, when Israel remembers the exodus, so John's mention of grass, loaves, a mountain, a sea, and manna is deliberate. The crowd wants to make him king by force, and he withdraws, which shows what kind of Messiah they were hoping for. "It is I" in 6:20 is literally "I am" (ego eimi), the divine name used in Exodus 3:14, and the first of John's seven "I am" sayings with a predicate, "I am the bread of life," comes at 6:35. The manna story is in Exodus 16, and the crowd's challenge, "Give us a sign," comes right after they have been fed. Jesus' words about eating his flesh and drinking his blood are among the hardest in the Gospels. Readers have long linked them to the Eucharist; others read them as about believing and receiving him. The phrase "the flesh profits nothing" in 6:63 is also debated. Capernaum's synagogue was the town's meeting place. Peter's confession in John 6:68-69 is the counterpart of his confession at Caesarea Philippi in the other Gospels. Jesus' remark about "a devil" among the twelve points to Judas, whom John is the Gospel most critical of.

people.note: Feeds the crowd, walks on the sea, and teaches that he is the bread of life.
Asked where to buy bread, and says it can't be done.
Brings a boy with five loaves and two fish.
Want to make him king, and then follow him to Capernaum.
Murmur at his claim to have come down from heaven.
Find the saying too hard and go back.
Named as the one who will betray him.

questions: John says Jesus asked Philip to test him, "for he knew what he would do." What is the test for?
The crowd came for loaves and Jesus talks about bread from heaven. What are they hungry for?
Many disciples leave after the "hard saying." What do you think was hard about it?
Peter says, "To whom would we go?" How is that different from a confident declaration?

words.note: "Our fathers ate the manna in the wilderness" (6:31, 6:49, 6:58).
"The bread which I will give is my flesh" (6:51-56, 6:63).
"This is the work of God, that you believe" (6:29, 6:35-47, 6:64-69).
"The sign he had done" and "What sign do you do?" (6:2, 6:14, 6:26, 6:30).
